_comment: TEMPLATE -- copy to songs.json and point it at your own audio.
cp tests/regression/songs.example.json tests/regression/songs.json
songs.json is gitignored, so your own file list never leaves your machine.
This template is committed, so a fresh clone always has something to copy.
TOP-LEVEL KEYS
audio_root   folder your 'file' paths are relative to (absolute paths also work)
output_dir   where DrumScript writes; it has no --output-dir flag, so this
must match what it actually uses ('outputs')
archive_dir  where dated run folders are kept
run_log      log the combined output is appended to
extra_files  repo-relative files copied into every run folder, so the
results travel with whatever context you want beside them
PER-ENTRY KEYS
name          output basename DrumScript will produce (<name>_transcription.json).
Must be unique, and must match the audio file's stem.
file          path relative to audio_root, or an absolute path
kind          'track'      -- a full song. No known-correct answer, so it is
compared against a previous run, never asserted.
'single_hit' -- one isolated drum or cymbal. Has a known answer,
so it is asserted.
python_flags  flags for the python interpreter itself, e.g. ['-W', 'ignore', '-B']
args          flags for drumscript.main, e.g. ['--rudiment']
expect        single_hit only: the exact instruments list expected
expect_events single_hit only: exact number of onsets expected (usually 1)
min_events    track only: a floor, to catch a track silently producing nothing
VALID INSTRUMENT LABELS
kick, snare, hi_hat_closed, hi_hat_open, low_tom, mid_tom, high_tom, crash, ride
If you do not know what a file SHOULD classify as, make it a 'track'. It will
then be compared against your previous run rather than asserted against a
label you had to guess.
